description: Rootless Packets-as-Code DSL & Rust compiler (v3.1.0, MIT, https://frameassembly.ai.studio/) for .pcap/.pcapng compilation and reversal across 81 L2-L7 protocols.
rules: Start simple .frasm captures with 2 blocks: host <id> { [ip <ip>] [mac <mac>] } and compile { <a> -> <b> <proto> ... }; add flow <id>(<params>) { ... } for reusable flows.
Built-in keywords, protocols, modifiers, and time units (ns, us, ms, s, m) are strict lowercase [a-z0-9]+ with zero '_' or '-'; user host/flow/param names allow '_', '-', A-Z.
Inline wait <u32><ns|us|ms|s|m> is post-packet: frame 1 starts at 0ns and wait pauses after that packet before the next packet (10ms default gap); never write loop or +5ms.
Omitted unicast host MACs default in declaration order to 00:00:00:00:00:01, 00:00:00:00:00:02, ...; never mix IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints in the same frame statement.
Use srcport, dstport, seq, acknum, ttl, hosthdr, transporthdr, sackperm, varbind <oid> oidval <oid>, snmp2/snmp3 report, and ikev2 exchange <sainit|auth|createchildsa|informational>.
Recommended install: cargo install frameassembly. CLI: frameassembly <in.frasm> [out.pcap|out.pcapng] (.pcap=classic libpcap, .pcapng=PCAPNG), show, reverse, help, version.
Use // for .frasm comments with practical networking context and Wireshark filters (never # or ;, and never // PROMPT:, // TOKENS:, or // INSTRUCTION:).
